title: Beetroot, Feta, and Walnut Salad
subtitle: Roasted beetroot with crumbled feta, toasted walnuts, and rocket
excerpt: Wedges of roasted beetroot on a bed of peppery rocket, scattered with crumbled feta, toasted walnuts, and a simple balsamic and olive oil dressing. A reliable combination that looks striking on the plate.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beetroot and feta became a standard British restaurant and café combination in the early 2000s, influenced by Mediterranean cooking. The earthiness of the beetroot, the saltiness of the feta, the bitterness of the rocket, and the crunch of the walnuts form a balanced combination. Pre-cooked vacuum-packed beetroot (not in vinegar) is a perfectly acceptable shortcut; roasted beetroot from scratch has more flavour.

content.text: Roast the beetroot wrapped in foil so it steams in its own moisture. Do not peel before roasting: the skin holds in the juices and slips off easily once cooked. Dress the beetroot while it is still slightly warm so it absorbs the dressing. Assemble the salad at the last moment.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Wrap the beetroot individually in foil and place on a baking sheet. Roast for 45 to 55 minutes until completely tender. Unwrap and cool slightly. Rub off the skins with kitchen paper (gloves help). Cut into wedges.
Whisk the balsamic vinegar, olive oil, and honey together with a pinch of salt. Toss the warm beetroot wedges in half the dressing.
Arrange the rocket on a large platter or individual plates. Place the beetroot wedges over the rocket. Scatter with crumbled feta and toasted walnuts. Drizzle with the remaining dressing.
